{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Step 1: Deduplicate by patient_id, keeping the row with highest sample_seq
# This ensures one row per patient, with the latest (highest sample_seq) assay
# Note: sample_seq is 1 or 2, so highest is 2

# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq (descending) to make deduplication easier
df_sorted = df.sort_values(['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Deduplicate: keep first (i.e., highest sample_seq) row per patient
df_dedup = df_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Step 2: Filter for SEVERE disease
severe_only = df_dedup[df_dedup['severity'] == 'severe']

# Step 3: Exclude rows where biomarker_baseline == -999 (QC failure)
severe_valid = severe_only[severe_only['biomarker_baseline'] != -999]

# Step 4: Check batch-B unit error
# The data dictionary says: assay_batch == 'B' reports in µg/L, not ng/mL
# So we must divide batch-B values by 10 to convert to ng/mL
# Note: this applies only to biomarker_baseline (as per the data dictionary)

# Create a copy to avoid modifying original
severe_clean = severe_valid.copy()
severe_clean.loc[severe_clean['assay_batch'] == 'B', 'biomarker_baseline'] = \
    severe_clean.loc[severe_clean['assay_batch'] == 'B', 'biomarker_baseline'] / 10

# Step 5: Compute mean baseline biomarker value (in ng/mL)
mean_baseline = severe_clean['biomarker_baseline'].mean()

# Print result
print(f'Mean baseline biomarker value (ng/mL) among patients with SEVERE disease: {mean_baseline}')"}
